final_candidates.decision_summary: Strongest AlphaMissense damaging signal; C61 is a RING zinc-coordinating cysteine, so its loss disrupts BRCA1 E3/repair function via a well-defined mechanism while leaving most of the protein intact.
Very high pathogenic-LOF prediction and mutation of a second RING zinc-ligand cysteine gives a coherent loss-of-function mechanism with minimal global structural perturbation.
High AlphaMissense score at the BRCT phospho-recognition site supports abolishing phosphopeptide-dependent repair signaling while preserving overall BRCT domain architecture.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 are clearly separated by the aligned LOF-pathogenicity proxy with strong mechanistic support, so additional evidence is unlikely to change the ranking.

history.rationale: Classic pathogenic RING-domain zinc-ligand mutation; abolishes BARD1 interaction and ubiquitin ligase activity, causing loss of DNA repair function.

C61 is a zinc-coordinating cysteine in the RING domain; substitution abolishes Zn binding and disrupts the BRCA1-BARD1 E3 complex, a classic pathogenic LOF mechanism (e.g., C61G is a known pathogenic variant).
AlphaMissense is the aligned LOF-pathogenicity proxy and gives the strongest damaging signal; C61 is also a known RING zinc-ligand context, supporting loss of BRCA1 E3/repair activity.
RING zinc-coordinating cysteine; substitution disrupts the RING fold locally and abolishes E3 ligase activity, a well-documented pathogenic LOF mechanism.
Second RING zinc-coordinating cysteine; same LOF mechanism as C61G.
Very high damaging prediction and mutation of a RING zinc-coordinating cysteine provide a coherent LOF mechanism while leaving most of BRCA1 unchanged.
Known pathogenic BRCT-domain variant that disrupts phospho-peptide binding pocket of the N-terminal BRCT repeat, abolishing damage-signaling interactions.
BRCT1 hydrophobic-core substitution; disrupts phosphopeptide-binding pocket of the BRCT repeats critical for DNA-damage response.
High AlphaMissense score in the BRCT region supports impaired phosphopeptide-dependent repair signaling with plausible preservation of overall domain architecture.
Recurrent pathogenic BRCT variant; Arg1699 contacts phosphoserine of binding partners and its loss abolishes BRCT phospho-recognition required for repair foci.
R1699 contacts the phosphate of pSer ligands in BRCT; R1699Q/W are well-established pathogenic variants abolishing BRCT binding.
Pathogenic proxy is positive but the lowest among retained pathogenic candidates; keep as a lower-tier alternative at the same position.
Bulky hydrophobic substitution at the BRCT phospho-binding Arg; strongly destabilizes the pSer-recognition interface while domain core folding is largely retained.
Alternative substitution at the BRCT phosphate anchor; strong disruption expected.
Clearly damaging but weaker than the leading RING/BRCT candidates, so retained as backup rather than promoted.
Pathogenic C-terminal BRCT variant that perturbs the BRCT hydrophobic core/interface and abolishes BRCA1 transcriptional/repair function.
BRCT2 core residue; M1775R is a known pathogenic variant that destabilizes the BRCT tandem.
Damaging score is comparable to S1655F and the BRCT location makes it a strong functional-LOF candidate; confidence remains limited by proxy-model uncertainty.
Conserved BRCT-repeat residue; substitution may impair BRCT fold/recognition, considered as a comparative LOF candidate.
BRCT1/BRCT2 inter-repeat interface residue; moderate-confidence LOF hypothesis.
AlphaMissense classifies this as benign, directly opposing the LOF objective; remove from active consideration.

rejection.reason: AlphaMissense classifies this as benign, directly opposing the LOF objective; remove from active consideration.

history.rationale: Proline insertion into RING zinc-binding region should disrupt local structure and ligase activity; speculative but plausible LOF driver.
RING-domain proline insertion disrupting local fold; lower confidence, may destabilize rather than preserve folding.

Phenotype score is very high, so it moves upward despite lower initial prior; I keep it below C61G/C64G because Pro may impose more local conformational disruption than desired for folding preservation.
